item.title: The squared antipode of a twisted function algebra is locally unipotent
item.description: arXiv:2611.33512v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a proalgebraic group over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $F:{\rm Rep}(G)\to {\rm Vect}(k)$ be a dimension-preserving tensor functor, possibly nonsymmetric. We prove that a tensor automorphism $T$ of $F$ is locally unipotent if and only if its trace on $F(V)$ equals ${\rm dim} V$ for every $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$. Applied to the Drinfeld element of a dual twisted function algebra $(\mathcal{O}(G)^J)^*$, this proves our conjecture from 2000 that the square of the antipode in $\mathcal{O}(G)^J$ is locally unipotent (arXiv:0002128). Without the trace assumption, we show that for any $V\in {\rm Rep}(G)$ the eigenvalues of $T$ on $F(V)$ determine, modulo roots of unity, its eigenvalues on $F(\mathbb{S}^\nu V)$ for every Schur functor $\mathbb{S}^\nu$. The proof combines the Koszul identity, polynomial growth of symmetric powers, Fourier inversion, and congruences for Newton sums.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Etingof, Shlomo Gelaki

item.title: Link invariants from charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.33552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Turaev's enhanced Yang--Baxter operators produce invariants of oriented links from solutions of the Yang--Baxter equation. If the enhancing endomorphism is diagonal with generic eigenvalues, Turaev's compatibility condition forces the Yang--Baxter operator $R$ to be charge-conserving, that is, to send each $e_i\otimes e_j$ into the span of $e_i\otimes e_j$ and $e_j\otimes e_i$. Charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators were classified by Martin and Rowell. Building on their classification, we determine all enhancements of charge-conserving Yang--Baxter operators with diagonal enhancing endomorphism, and we identify the resulting link invariants. The link invariant associated with such an enhancement is a sum over the colourings of the components of the link by the connected components of $R$, in which each monochromatic sublink contributes a specialization of the HOMFLY--PT polynomial and different colours interact only through linking numbers. Every such state sum arises in this way.
item.dc:creator: C\'esar Galindo, Laura Rodr\'iguez Sierra

item.title: Proof of a cardinality conjecture for the correction terms in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom
item.description: arXiv:2611.33597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a conjecture due to Kato and Sagaki (arXiv:2604.04476) concerning the cardinality of sets of directed paths in the quantum Bruhat graph that occur in the quantum $K$-theoretic divisor axiom for the full flag manifolds in the quasi-minuscule case. We prove that the cadinality is equal to one or even, and its signed sum vanishes in the latter case. Consequently, the cancellation-free divisor axiom obtained by Kato and Sagaki under this conjecture holds unconditionally. The proof uses Schremmer's results on affine Bruhat order and Demazure products, together with a theorem that we prove for arbitrary Coxeter groups.
item.dc:creator: Mizuki Takahashi

item.title: Nonzero central quotients of the Virasoro enveloping algebra are simple
item.description: arXiv:2611.33310v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra that the central quotient $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$ of the universal enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra is simple for all $c \neq 0$. We extend the result to the $N=1$ super-Virasoro algebras. Our proof reveals a new connection between enveloping algebras and polynomial identity algebras. Although the enveloping algebra itself does not satisfy a polynomial identity, the adjoint action on each filtered piece does satisfy a standard identity. In particular, the Witt algebra $W$, as an adjoint module over itself, satisfies the standard identity $\mathrm{St}_4$, whereas $\mathrm{Vir}$ fails by a nonzero multiple of the central charge. Propagating this gap through the PBW filtration of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})/(z-c)$, for every nonscalar element, we construct an alternating adjoint operator that lowers its order by exactly one. As applications, we compute the annihilators of all representations with nonzero central character, prove a strengthened form of Etingof's conjecture on nonsplit extensions of $W$-modules, and reduce the classification of prime ideals of $\mathrm{U}(\mathrm{Vir})$ to those of $\mathrm{U}(W)$.
item.dc:creator: Tuan Anh Pham, Haijun Tan

item.title: P{\l}onka bi-magmas and the set-theoretic Yang--Baxter equation
item.description: arXiv:2305.14138v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new variety of universal algebras with two binary operations, called \emph{P{\l}onka bi-magmas}, and use them to construct novel solutions to the set-theoretic Yang-Baxter (YB) equation. We establish explicit structural and classification results for P{\l}onka bi-magmas, which allow for a detailed study of the induced families of YB-solutions. In particular, we identify and classify several naturally arising classes of YB-solutions from the universal algebra perspective, including the so-called bi-connected and ideal-simple ones. For instance, we prove that there are only countably many isomorphism classes of induced YB-solutions which are ideal-simple, and characterize them in terms of the odometer transformations familiar from ergodic theory. In particular, if $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, then the number of isomorphism classes of all the induced ideal-simple YB-solutions on $X$ is equal to the sum of all divisors of $n$.
item.dc:creator: A. L. Agore, A. Chirvasitu, G. Militaru

item.title: On Frobenius-Schur exponent bounds
item.description: arXiv:2404.06643v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study bounds on the Frobenius--Schur exponent of spherical fusion categories in terms of their global dimension, generalizing bounds from the representation theory of finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebras. Our main result is that if the Frobenius--Schur exponent of a modular fusion category is a power of a prime $p$, then it is bounded by the norm of its global dimension when $p$ is odd, and by four times the norm of its global dimension when $p=2$; these bounds are optimal. Moreover, it is bounded by a constant multiple of the geometric mean of the Galois conjugates of its global dimension, which is much smaller when the global dimension is irrational, and a bound of this type is proven for each prime power dividing the Frobenius--Schur exponent of an arbitrary modular or spherical fusion category. Under pseudounitarity, we describe all modular and spherical fusion categories whose Frobenius--Schur exponent is a prime power and at least the norm (respectively, the square of the norm) of their global dimension, using a classification of modular fusion categories of Frobenius--Perron dimension $p^n$ for $n\leq5$.
item.dc:creator: Agustina Czenky, Julia Plavnik, Andrew Schopieray

item.title: Symmetry of some noncommutative sphere algebras
item.description: arXiv:2602.06946v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Two known $q$-deformed (or `quantum') $7$-spheres, both denoted $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ in the literature, may be distinguished by the presence or absence of symmetry under $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$. The quaternionic version of $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ has been shown by Brain and Landi to support such a symmetry. Here we show that this is not the case for the older $\mathbb{S}^7_q$ introduced by Vaksman and Soibelman: and as a consequence, these quantum $7$-spheres are not isomorphic.
item.dc:creator: William J. Ugalde, Joseph C. V\'arilly

item.title: New approaches to finite generation of cohomology rings
item.description: arXiv:1911.04552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In support variety theory, representations of a finite dimensional (Hopf) algebra $A$ can be studied geometrically by associating any representation of $A$ to an algebraic variety using the cohomology ring of $A$. An essential assumption in this theory is the finite generation condition for the cohomology ring of $A$ and that for the corresponding modules. In this paper, we introduce various approaches to study the finite generation condition. First, for any finite dimensional Hopf algebra $A$, we show that the finite generation condition on $A$-modules can be replaced by a condition on any affine commutative $A$-module algebra $R$ under the assumption that $R$ is integral over its invariant subring $R^A$. Next, we use a spectral sequence argument to show that a finite generation condition holds for certain filtered, smash and crossed product algebras in positive characteristic if the related spectral sequences collapse. Finally, if $A$ is defined over a number field over the rationals, we construct another finite dimensional Hopf algebra $A'$ over a finite field, where $A$ can be viewed as a deformation of $A'$, and prove that if the finite generation condition holds for $A'$, then the same condition holds for $A$.
item.dc:creator: Van C. Nguyen, Xingting Wang, Sarah Witherspoon

item.title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
item.description: arXiv:2509.10603v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use a 2-categorical version of (de-)equivariantization to classify (3+1)d topological orders with a finite $G$-symmetry. In particular, we argue that (3+1)d fermionic topological order with $G$-symmetry correspond to $\mathbf{2SVect}$-enriched $G$-crossed braided fusion 2-categories. We then show that the categorical data necessary to define these theories agrees with that arising from a fermionic generalization of the Wang-Wen-Witten construction of bosonic topological theories with $G$-symmetry saturating an anomaly. More generally, we also explain how 2-categorical (de-) equivariantization yields a classification of all braided fusion 2-categories.
item.dc:creator: Thibault D. D\'ecoppet, Matthew Yu

item.title: Free wreath products by finite group duals
item.description: arXiv:2512.11477v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb G$ be a compact quantum group and let $\Lambda$ be a finite group. We study $\mathbb W(\mathbb G,\Lambda):=\mathbb G\wr_{*,\beta_\Lambda}\widehat{\Lambda}$, a natural family parallel to Bichon's free wreath products $\mathbb G\wr_*S_N^+$. We obtain an explicit formula for the Haar state of $\mathbb W(\mathbb G,\Lambda)$. Under natural Kac-type factoriality assumptions, we also derive central decompositions of the associated von Neumann and reduced C*-algebras, with full ${\rm II}_1$-factor and simple unique-trace summands.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Fima, Yigang Qiu

item.title: A Syntactic Approach to Ulmer's Bialgebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.19587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ulmer proposed to view a bialgebraic structure on an object $x$ as a structure map $f\colon Fx\to Gx$ satisfying an equation $\alpha_{(x,f)} = \beta_{(x,f)}$ of natural transformations. This perspective is powerful enough to account for many algebraic and coalgebraic structures, such as varieties of universal algebra, categories of algebras over a PROP, an operad or a monad. We develop Ulmer's bialgebras within a $2$-categorical setting with PIE limits, where structure maps are abstracted by inserters and their equations by equifiers. A syntax of signatures, theories and models is then used to produce these bialgebraic structures. The syntax of the commutative diagrams defining Hopf algebras can be used, as is, to define the $0$-cell of Hopf algebras within any symmetric pseudomonoid in a $2$-category with PIE limits. In this setting, we show that lax morphisms of models induce morphisms between the objects of algebras, extending the classical result lifting a lax monoidal functor to a functor between the categories of internal monoids. Since the construction of the object of bialgebras is expressed entirely in terms of PIE limits, we show that Kan extensions, accessibility, local presentability, orthogonal factorization systems, regularity, and Barr-exactness lift along the construction under suitable assumptions. A bi-dense class of objects allows us to transfer monadicity and local presentability results to formal settings. Finally, we construct a bi-dense class of $\V$-categories with at most three objects, where $\V$ is any monoidal category with an absorbing initial object.
item.dc:creator: David Forsman

item.title: Partial $F$-invariants and cluster categorifications
item.description: arXiv:2609.08781v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $F$-invariant in cluster algebras is a combinatorial invariant that unifies the $E$-invariant from additive categorification and the $\mathfrak{d}$-invariant from monoidal categorification. In this paper, we study its refinement, the partial $F$-invariant, and establish its mutation formula under changes of the initial seed. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Reading, which asserts that the non-compatible cluster variables can be separated by sign-coherence of $g$-vectors upon varying the initial seed. We further show that, for cluster monomials, the partial $F$-invariants coincide with both the partial $E$-invariants for reachable decorated representations of quivers with potentials and the pole orders of normalized $R$-matrices (or partial $\mathfrak{d}$-invariants) for finite-dimensional reachable simple modules over quantum affine algebras. As consequences, we obtain a combinatorial formula for the pole orders for reachable simple modules in terms of $q$-characters; we verify the conjectural explicit formula for the pole orders between Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules.
item.dc:creator: Peigen Cao, Ryo Fujita, Kota Murakami
